From 0972252450f90db56dd5415a20e2aec21a08d036 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Arun Easi <aeasi@marvell.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Mar 2022 01:25:56 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: qla2xxx: Fix crash during module load unload test

During purex packet handling the driver was incorrectly freeing a
pre-allocated structure. Fix this by skipping that entry.

System crashed with the following stack during a module unload test.

Call Trace:
	sbitmap_init_node+0x7f/0x1e0
	sbitmap_queue_init_node+0x24/0x150
	blk_mq_init_bitmaps+0x3d/0xa0
	blk_mq_init_tags+0x68/0x90
	blk_mq_alloc_map_and_rqs+0x44/0x120
	blk_mq_alloc_set_map_and_rqs+0x63/0x150
	blk_mq_alloc_tag_set+0x11b/0x230
	scsi_add_host_with_dma.cold+0x3f/0x245
	qla2x00_probe_one+0xd5a/0x1b80 [qla2xxx]

Call Trace with slub_debug and debug kernel:
	kasan_report_invalid_free+0x50/0x80
	__kasan_slab_free+0x137/0x150
	slab_free_freelist_hook+0xc6/0x190
	kfree+0xe8/0x2e0
	qla2x00_free_device+0x3bb/0x5d0 [qla2xxx]
	qla2x00_remove_one+0x668/0xcf0 [qla2xxx]

Fixes: 62e9dd177732 ("scsi: qla2xxx: Change in PUREX to handle FPIN ELS requests")

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
index 58c83525f006..9c4f2b38b34e 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
@@ -3901,6 +3901,8 @@ qla24xx_free_purex_list(struct purex_list *list)
 	spin_lock_irqsave(&list->lock, flags);
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(item, next, &list->head, list) {
 		list_del(&item->list);
+		if (item == &item->vha->default_item)
+			continue;
 		kfree(item);
 	}
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&list->lock, flags);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c`**
   - A conditional check was added in the `qla24xx_free_purex_list` function to skip freeing a specific pre-allocated structure. The check ensures that if the current item being processed is the same as `&item->vha->default_item`, the function will continue to the next iteration without calling `kfree(item)`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug that caused a crash during module load/unload tests by preventing the driver from incorrectly freeing a pre-allocated structure. This change is directly related to the reported issue, as it ensures that the specific structure is not freed, thus avoiding the invalid memory access that led to the crash. The patch is a fix for a previous change identified by the commit hash `62e9dd177732`, which altered the handling of PUREX to manage FPIN ELS requests. The addition of the conditional check is a corrective measure to maintain stability during the module's lifecycle.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the driver incorrectly freeing a pre-allocated structure during the handling of purex packets, specifically when the structure was still in use, leading to invalid memory access and a crash during module unload tests.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline void
 qla24xx_free_purex_list(struct purex_list *list)
 {
 	struct purex_item *item, *next;
 	ulong flags;
 
 	spin_lock_irqsave(&list->lock, flags);
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(item, next, &list->head, list) {
 		list_del(&item->list);
+		if (item == &item->vha->default_item)
+			continue;
 		kfree(item);
 	}
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&list->lock, flags);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
list_del(&item->list);
kfree(item);
```
Reason:
The driver was incorrectly freeing a pre-allocated structure (`item`) that was still in use during the handling of purex packets. This led to an invalid memory access when the structure was accessed after being freed, causing a crash during module unload tests.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (item == &item->vha->default_item)
    continue;
```
Reason:
This addition checks if the `item` being processed is the default item associated with the virtual host adapter (`vha`). If it is, the code skips the freeing of that item, preventing the invalid memory access and subsequent crash during module unload tests.
